substeps.label: Amerex B570
substeps.caption: The lab's own Class D extinguisher: 30 lb of Super D, a sodium-chloride powder that crusts over burning metal. Built from Amerex's datasheet and render.

substeps.label: Amerex B570
substeps.caption: Its parts, as Amerex draws them: a chrome-plated brass valve, a hose in a turn and a half, a soft-flow applicator held in two lattice bands.

substeps.label: The valve
substeps.caption: Chrome-plated brass. The gauge reads in the green; a large-loop stainless pin and a red tamper seal hold the lever.

substeps.label: The applicator
substeps.caption: Its soft-flow cup lays the powder on gently, so it never blasts burning metal into the air; it comes off for a straight stream.

substeps.label: On a post at each station
substeps.caption: Hung from its own hook so its lever is at 826 mm and its hose at 1047 mm: NFPA 10's 42 in for a unit over 40 lb. CLASS D signs at 60 and 80 in, a keep-clear square.

substeps.label: Amerex 811 vehicle bracket
substeps.caption: Heavy duty, box type, sold for 30 lb Class D units: 17.5 in tall, rubber-lined, with a quick-release strap.

substeps.label: Strapped in
substeps.caption: It stands on the foot plate, its back on the bushings; the strap goes round above the lower band, clear of the label, and latches over centre.

substeps.label: On every MiR250
substeps.caption: Each MiR250 carries one in an 811 on its cabinet's aisle side, under the arm and over its scanners' plane, wherever the robot works. Its turning circle stays 494 mm.

substeps.label: Available for use
substeps.caption: Anyone near the robot takes it: throw the strap's latch, lift it off the foot plate and go. It is 50 lb, so it hangs low.

substeps.label: Where the most powder is
substeps.caption: An Amerex 680R: 150 lb of the same agent, argon-regulated to 125 psi, on 36 in non-sparking wheels, at the rePowder and the EOS. A 50 lb pail of it with a scoop beside.
